title: The Kitchen Clock Is Wrong
imageAlt: The Kitchen Clock Is Wrong by Dorado Project: two cups and wooden chairs in a kitchen opening onto an empty railway platform, with a wall clock and blue coat
description: A seven-track progressive rock concept album about the conversations we keep putting off — and the ordinary day in which somebody finally stays to listen.
genreLabel: Progressive Rock / Psychedelic Rock / Art Rock
statusNote: In production. The final release details are being prepared; no release date or streaming availability has been announced.
trackStatusNote: Part of an album in production. The verified listening link will be added after a release is confirmed.
pageTitle: The Kitchen Clock Is Wrong — Dorado Project
metaDescription: Explore The Kitchen Clock Is Wrong, a seven-track progressive rock concept album by Dorado Project about work, missed conversations and making time to listen.
story: “Five minutes before you go?” There is a train to catch, work to finish and a good reason to leave. By evening, the unanswered request has become harder to ignore.

The Kitchen Clock Is Wrong follows one ordinary day through a kitchen, a crowded train, an office building and the rooms people return to. Its seven tracks look at the distance that grows when conversation is always saved for later. The person left waiting has her own account of the day, and her own limits.

Two instrumental chapters make room around five songs about borrowed time, public lives and private decisions. A train leaves without its passenger. A name is asked. A chair moves across the floor. These small actions carry the story toward an ending that leaves the conversation open.
Dorado Project brings that domestic story into progressive rock, psychedelic rock and art rock. The album ends at the kitchen table, with an answer that begins by listening.

tracks.title: Threshold of Morning
tracks.description: Threshold of Morning by Dorado Project, from The Kitchen Clock Is Wrong. An instrumental opening to a house before the day gathers speed.
tracks.story: An instrumental opening to a house before the day gathers speed. It sets the scene for a request that will return later: a little time together before somebody leaves.
tracks.creativeDirection: The opening was conceived as a small instrumental threshold rather than a full-band climax. Its place in the story is the few moments before a familiar morning request.

tracks.creativeDirection: The written scene begins with two cups and an unfinished exchange, then follows the narrator onto the train. Real responsibilities and habitual avoidance occupy the same journey.

tracks.theme: Another voice · waiting has its limits
tracks.description: The Weight of Quiet by Dorado Project, from The Kitchen Clock Is Wrong. The person at home speaks for herself.
tracks.story: The person at home speaks for herself. She turns off the radio, puts a pan on the stove and leaves a chair beside her, while making clear that she will not keep her own life on hold.
tracks.creativeDirection: The written female perspective has its own concerns and boundaries. Everyday acts in the kitchen continue while she decides what she needs to say, without waiting indefinitely.

tracks.story: An automatic yes is erased from a message. The narrator lets a train leave and makes the call he has been avoiding, with no polished explanation ready when somebody answers.
tracks.creativeDirection: The narrator’s interrupted routine becomes a decision: a message is erased, a train leaves, and a call is made. The planned arrangement gives this turning point the album’s physical release.

pageTitle: Frequency Flashback — 20 Original Songs | Dorado Project
metaDescription: Explore Frequency Flashback by Dorado Project: 20 original Dutch and English songs with pop, dance, rock and soul, inspired by the variety of classic hits compilations.
story: Frequency Flashback starts from the pleasure of a favourite compilation: the next song can bring a different voice, a new rhythm or an unexpected change of mood. Its twenty original songs take that sense of variety into a new Dorado Project album.

Ten Dutch-language songs and ten English-language songs share the running order. Different vocal characters, bands and arrangements belong to the creative brief; Dorado Project remains the credited artist throughout.

The collection draws on the energy of 1990s and 2000s pop culture without using existing hits, samples or impersonations. These are new songs, with room for the dance floor, a guitar band, a soulful chorus and a quieter final stretch.

Created with AI tools under the direction of Rutger Kussendrager. The track notes describe the creative direction rather than claiming that a particular sound or performance has already been verified.
